# Now 2.13.32
- The line-to-line transition in the full-screen view is quicker. The highlight was taking longer to settle than the text underneath it took to move, so the change felt like it was playing in slow motion.

# Now 2.13.31
- Smoother line-to-line transitions in the full-screen view, from three fixes: - The playback clock is now monotonic. Position samples from the browser arrive about once a second and can land slightly behind the running clock, which nudged it backward just enough to re-select the previous line at a line boundary and make the word-by-word highlight twitch back mid-line. The clock now only moves forward, unless it moves back far enough to mean a real seek. - The lyric list no longer re-renders on unrelated playback updates. It was rebuilding every visible line, sometimes mid-transition, each time a position sample arrived. - The focus effect no longer re-renders every line on every frame of a transition, and the highlight now settles once instead of overshooting.

# Now 2.13.30
- Cut CPU use during playback. Checking whether the browser is still running was asking the system for information about every running app several times a second, which blocked the interface briefly each time. That answer is now cached and refreshed only when an app actually launches or quits. - The lyric focus effect no longer applies to lines far from the one playing. Those lines are already faded almost to nothing, so the effect was invisible there while still costing rendering work on every line change.
